sources.title: Prolific tech analyst Dan Ives is exiting Wedbush for a new venture
sources.speaker: Dan Ives, interviewed by Yun Li (CNBC)

sources.excerpt: "It's been a phenomenal eight years at Wedbush," Ives said in an interview. "But in looking at the next opportunity, it's to create a modern merchant bank with great partners, long-term capital and something I think will change the way Wall Street looks at investment banks." ... sources.title: 'I'm an example of what I've preached': Dan Ives knows AI has a 'PR problem' but it led to his massive career change after 25 years on Wall Street
sources.speaker: Dan Ives, interviewed on Zoom by Nick Lichtenberg (Fortune business editor)
sources.locator: Paragraphs 1-3 (Margaritaville shirt; "never built anything"; "off the treadmill"); paragraphs 11-12 (Kool-Aid framing; "bingo card"; "next decade"); paragraphs 14-16 (Long Island dress; YOLO; parents); paragraphs 18-19 ("AI has a PR problem"; third inning; Vegas Strip 1955)
sources.excerpt: "As an analyst I always talk about companies, whether good or bad, what they've done. But I've never built anything," he said. ... "I wanted to get off the treadmill and actually build something myself." ... "Sometimes you can make choices that might — you think they're right and ultimately, you look back and you should have gone left instead of right or whatever … but I'm not gonna like live life like that." ... "I had great parents that passed away young and I'm not afraid to stumble." ... "put things (and work) in perspective and only one life to live. I am 51 today but I view life through a different lens than I did when I was 40 years old after going through this nightmare." ... "We're going to look back on this period," he said, "and realize this is building the Vegas Strip in 1955." ... Ives said he knows the proof will be in the pudding. "This is not about doing it for a year, two years," he said. "It's about building something special for the next decade."
sources.context: The most personal interview found: a Zoom conversation several weeks after the Wedbush exit. Reports that from 2015 through 2025 his father had Alzheimer's and his mother Parkinson's; his mother died at 70 in 2020 and his father at 79 in 2025. The Kool-Aid paragraph is ambiguous: "He agreed" may refer to the framing or to the surprise of the moment, so do not write that he admitted drinking the Kool-Aid. The writer offers both a skeptical and a "charitable" read. Edit stage (2026-10-24): rechecked the saved page. Fortune's own narration says losing his parents "gave him a tolerance for calculated risk" and "when it comes to calculated risk, he likes to go for it"; "25 years" is Fortune's narration ("the better part of 25 years", "after 25 years covering other people's companies"), not his words. The Kool-Aid/"more charitable read" pair is the writer's framing; the edit no longer reports it. Repair stage (2026-10-24): paragraph 12 narration, 'Ives said he knows the proof will be in the pudding,' is now reported as Fortune's wording (C176).

claims.claim: Daniel H. Ives grew up on Long Island, studied finance at Penn State's Smeal College of Business (B.S.), spent a few years in corporate finance at HBO in New York, earned an MBA at the University of Maryland's Smith School (MBA 2000), then spent about 16 years as a technology research analyst at FBR Capital Markets.

claims.claim: In February 2016 he left sell-side research for an operating role at Synchronoss Technologies (reported by NJBIZ as SVP of finance and corporate development, leading global investor relations; the SEC calls him EVP of Investor Relations). TWST's 2020 bio calls Synchronoss a mobile cloud vendor.
claims.passage: In February 2016 he left sell-side research for an operating job at Synchronoss Technologies, a mobile cloud company, where he led investor relations.
claims.inference: His first move out of research; it ended with termination per the SEC (C101). Absent from most of his later career accounts in the interviews opened for this page (C103).
claims.alternative: Leaving research for an operator job is also an ordinary career experiment; "terminated" comes from the SEC findings, and no account from Ives explains the departure. Do not speculate on why he left FBR or why he was terminated.

claims.claim: The SEC order says Ives was Synchronoss's EVP of Investor Relations from about February 2016 to mid-2017, "when he was terminated," and gives no reason.
claims.passage: The SEC says he was terminated in mid-2017. Its order does not say why.
claims.inference: Regulator's statement of fact inside a settled order; Barron's repeats it ("fired from the Synchronoss job in 2017, according to an SEC filing").
claims.alternative: No account from Ives or Synchronoss explains the termination; the article does not link it to the 2016 deal.

claims.claim: On 2022-06-07 the SEC entered a settled cease-and-desist order. It found that Ives, with other company officials, helped negotiate one reseller transaction closed on December 31, 2016, promised the counterparty it would not suffer a loss, and that Synchronoss improperly recognized about $3.6 million of revenue from it (Exchange Act Section 13(b)(5), Rule 13b2-1).
claims.passage: In a settled 2022 order, the SEC found that he helped negotiate one year-end 2016 deal, promising the other company it would not suffer a loss, through which Synchronoss improperly recognized about $3.6 million in revenue.
claims.inference: A regulator's settled findings about one transaction at a company later forced to restate about $190 million of revenue. FINRA records that the order is not based on anti-fraud provisions. Relevant to the portrait as context for later conflict-of-interest scrutiny and as a chapter he does not discuss.
claims.alternative: Settled findings are neither admitted nor denied and are not binding on others. Others at the company approved the effort. Do not call it fraud, do not imply the restatement was his doing, and do not draw psychological conclusions from it. If used, state the findings in one or two attributed, dated sentences with the settlement terms.

claims.claim: Without admitting or denying the SEC's findings, Ives paid a $15,000 civil penalty and undertook for three years not to participate as a salesperson in transactions involving side agreements or sales of $10,000 or more (plus 30 hours of revenue-recognition training, not mentioned in the draft).

type_hypothesis.against: (1) Brand and recognition fluency is strong and explicit: he credits his clothes with his "global success", says people who do not know his stock calls know him as "the person who wears the funky shirts on CNBC", says he brought "his brand" to Yorkville Ives, and his name is on two ETFs, the AI 30, a fund and a firm (C13, C125, C94). (2) In the NY Post he jokes that a conventional jacket was taken "very bearishly" and enjoys being copied, so the clothes are audience-facing as well as mood regulation (C124). (3) After the January 2026 cover story he ran a recognisable image-repair sequence: CNBC the next business day (C113, C82), a friendly podcast defence (C25), new X disclosures (C151), the Eightco exit six weeks later (C83), and a July approach to the same reporters through his publicist (C152); meanwhile name-bearing vehicles kept coming (C127, C08, C72) (C122). (4) He tells a hard-work credibility story, toned his dress down for Wall Street and uses a publicist (C31, C11, C95). (5) Long tenures (about 16 and 8 years) and the 2019 downgrade's duty-to-clients register fit a credibility-guarding Three as well as or better than a Seven (C105, C104, C19). (6) His AI pitch about "being behind" and "build something myself" are achievement language as much as Seven language (C27, C157). (7) Work incentives explain much of the public bullishness and brand-building (C05, C45, C67). Most first-person material is promotional or friendly. (8) Results language at the start of the build: "You just have to convince people, you have to show them the results" (BI, July 15, 2026) and Fortune's "he knows the proof will be in the pudding" (C175, C176, C177). (9) Audience framing of the clothes in his own words: "If I dressed non-colorful and wore a Brooks Brothers suit, investors would view it extremely bearishly" (Advisor Upside, Aug. 12, 2025, S43) beside the NY Post "very bearishly" joke (C124). (10) Two months after "I needed to simplify", two more outside roles began (Innovation X advisory; Ives Ultra fund chairmanship, both 09/2026), which a Three's bigger stage explains as well as a Seven's options (C169, C179).
type_hypothesis.alternative_case: Three explains the career as a sustained build of an admired, recognisable brand: an outsider who worked weekends to earn credibility (C31); toned his dress down for Wall Street until he "ripped a Band-Aid off" (C11); credits the clothes with his "global success" and recognition (C13); brought "his brand" to the new firm and turned his name into products (C125, C94); and, when Barron's questioned his roles, repaired the image in the standard sequence (TV defence, disclosures, pruning the most criticised role, re-engaging the outlet once he had a launch) before moving to a bigger stage (C122). On this reading, "simplify" is a reputational retreat and the bank the next rung. Fear of being behind and "build something myself" fit a Three's competitive drive (C157).
type_hypothesis.discriminator: Repair stage (2026-10-24): no defensible discriminator yet; this is why status is insufficient_evidence. What does not discriminate: role accumulation, including the two September 2026 roles, and the post-Barron's repair sequence (C122, C123, C169). What leans Seven: his own account of what his choices do for him (clothes as mood and freedom before audience, C62, C63, C12; leaving research as getting off "the treadmill", C85; refusing to live by regret, C90, C126) and answering costs with possibilities (C115, C69, C72, C116, C75, C25, C86). The nearest dated split is 2022, when the green jacket drew "hundreds of messages" of mockery during his failed calls and he kept it, calling it comfort (C173, C174); but by then the jackets were his brand, so a Three also predicts keeping them (C172). What leans Three: results language at launch (C175-C177), audience framing of the clothes (C124, S43), brand fluency and name-bearing vehicles (C13, C94). A discriminator would be a dated choice where the motives part: a more interesting role taken at a cost to his visibility, or a bigger stage declined because it would constrain him; or his own or named-testimony account of why he left top-ranked research for Synchronoss investor relations in 2016 and returned via GBH Insights and Wedbush (C171). The Seven lead remains a medium-confidence working hypothesis, mostly self-report from friendly or promotional interviews (C158).
type_hypothesis.unexplained: (1) The 2016 move from research to an operating job at Synchronoss and its end in termination (per the SEC, no reason given) rarely appear in his own career accounts in the interviews opened for this page, though his FINRA filing lists the job and the SEC order; nothing in the record says what that chapter meant to him (C03, C101, C103). (2) The moral register of the 2019 Tesla downgrade (in translation, no longer able to look investors in the eye) reads as duty to clients and favours Three or another credibility-guarding type, and he held Neutral for two years (C19, C104). (3) Blocking reporters sits awkwardly beside "I'm like an open book", though that line referred to his public presence (C16). (4) Long tenures (16 and 8 years) are steadier than a scattered Seven; the novelty of the tech beat ("a chaotic environment ... I've thrived in") is a partial Seven explanation, and a long build fits Three as well (C105, C134). (5) Warmth and generosity in the testimony (C28, C32) leave a Two-flavoured element unexplained; wing calls are not needed and stay out of the argument. (6) The Innovation X advisory role (09/2026) and the Ives Ultra fund chairmanship (09/2026) began about two months after "I needed to simplify" and "110% focused"; FINRA gives hours (4 and 20 a month) but no reason or pay, and no source has him explaining them (C169, C170).
